claims.text: The intervention is a thermal pre-treatment of bulk HfNbTaTiZr at 800�b0C to 1200�b0C for a specified duration.
The thermal pre-treatment will increase short-range chemical ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
The thermal pre-treatment will enhance local lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Increased short-range order and local lattice distortion impede dislocation mobility.
Impeded dislocation mobility caused by the pre-treatment will increase elevated-temperature yield strength relative to the homogenized baseline.
The pre-treatment will alter elevated-temperature strain-hardening behavior relative to the homogenized baseline.
The pre-treatment will reduce the thermal expansion coefficient relative to the homogenized baseline.
The pre-treatment will shift elastic moduli at elevated temperatures relative to the homogenized baseline.
Resonant ultrasound spectroscopy can be used to determine elastic moduli.
Elevated-temperature elastic and plastic responses of refractory high-entropy alloys can be characterized experimentally, including yield behavior, lattice strain evolution, and elastic moduli.
Stress-strain behavior in high-entropy alloys can depend on temperature and strain rate.
The proposed mechanism and predicted responses will hold throughout 800�b0C to 1200�b0C without additional phase transformations or significant degradation.
Moderate strain rates permit atomic reordering without triggering additional phase transformations.
The magnitude of changes in yield strength, thermal expansion, and elastic moduli may depend on the precise treatment parameters and resulting microstructural evolution.
